==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-C0603-0008-001, Vorbereitung Frauenkongress, Delegierte Palm.jpg|thumb|Woman making a telephone call (1964).]]
[[File:Pandion haliaetus.ogg|thumb|Call of the [[osprey]] (bird).]]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:callen|tree=+}}
From {{inh|en|enm|callen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*callian|t=to call, shout}} and {{der|en|non|kalla|t=to call; shout; refer to as; name}}; both from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kalzōną|t=to call, shout}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*golH-so-|t=voice, cry}}, from {{m|ine-pro||*gel(H)-|to vocalize, call, shout}}.

* {{cog|nl|kallen|t=to chat, talk}}
* {{cog|nds-de|kallen|t=to speak, talk}}
* {{cog|de|kallen|t=to call}}
* {{cog|sv|kalla|t=to call, refer to, beckon}}

*  {{cog|da|kalde|t=to call, name}}
* {{cog|is|kalla|t=to call, shout, name}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+|+|+,~'d<l:archaic>}}

# {{lb|en|heading}} To [[reach out]] with one's [[voice]].
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[request#Verb|request]], [[summon]], or [[beckon]].
##: {{ux|en|That person is hurt; '''call''' for help!}}
##* {{RQ:Bunyan Pilgrim's Progress|reprint=1875|part=2|page=128|passage=So they '''called''' for Rooms; and he ſhewed them one for ''Christiana'' and her Children and ''Mercy'', and another for Mr. ''Great-heart'' and the old Gentleman.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[cry]] or [[shout]].
##: {{syn|en|holler|yell|Thesaurus:shout}}
##: ''"Supper's ready," '''call'''ed Dad from the kitchen.''
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing Q|act=III|scene=iii|page=42|passage=If you heare a child crie in the night you must '''call''' to the nurſe and bid her ſtil it.}}
##* {{RQ:Kipling Just So Stories|story=How the Alphabet was Made|stanza=5|page=169|passage=For far—oh, very far behind, / So far she cannot '''call''' to him, / Comes Tegumai alone to find / The daughter that was all to him!}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[utter]] in a [[loud]] or [[distinct]] voice.
##: {{co|en|to '''call''' the roll of a military company}}
##* {{RQ:John Gay Shepherd's Week|page=56|lines=47–50|passage=Not ballad-ſinger plac'd above the croud, / Sings with a note ſo ſhrilling ſweet and loud, / Nor pariſh clerk who '''calls''' the pſalm ſo clear, / Like Bowzybeus ſooths th' attentive ear.}}
## {{senseid|en|to telephone}}{{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[contact]] by [[telephone]].
##: {{syn|en|drop a line|ring<id:to telephone>|get on the horn|give someone a ring|give someone a bell|Thesaurus:telephone}}
##: {{ux|en|Why don’t you '''call''' me in the morning?}}
##: {{ux|en|Why don’t you '''call''' tomorrow?}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Edgar Rice Burroughs}}|title={{w|The Return of Tarzan}}|publisher=Ballantine Books|location=New York|year_published=1963|page=41|passage=There they waited until after eleven, then Paulvitch took down the receiver of their telephone. He '''called''' a number.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[rouse]] from [[sleep]]; to [[awaken]].
##: {{syn|en|wake up|Thesaurus:awaken}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Cymbeline|act=II|scene=ii|page=376|column=2|passage=Take not away the Taper, leaue it burning: / And if thou canſt awake by foure o’th’clock, / I prythee '''call''' me: Sleepe hath ceiz’d me wholly.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|jazz}} To [[request]] that one's [[band]] [[play]] (a particular [[tune]]).
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1997|journal=Saxophone Journal
|passage=They '''called''' ''I Got Rhythm'', and turned to me again for a solo, and I said what?}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Ken Vail|title=Duke's Diary
|passage=Jeff Castleman and Rufus Jones were in position when they went out, and he immediately '''called''' Satin Doll.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Clyde E. B. Bernhardt|title=I Remember: Eighty Years of Black Entertainment, Big Bands, and the Blues|publisher=University of Pennsylvania Press|isbn=9781512801781|page=98
|passage=I thought he forgot all about it, but late in the set he '''called''' ''St. Louis Blues''.}}
## {{lb|en|Yorkshire|transitive}} To [[scold]].
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1865|author=William Stott Banks|title=Wakefield Words|page=11
|passage=CALL 1 scold}}
# {{lb|en|heading|intransitive}} To [[visit]].
## To [[pay]] a ([[social]]) [[visit]] {{gloss|often used with "on", "round", or "at"; used by [[salesperson|salespeople]] with "again" to [[invite]] [[customer]]s to come again}}.
##: {{ux|en|We could always '''call''' on a friend.}}
##: {{ux|en|The engineer '''called''' round whilst you were away.}}
##* {{RQ:Temple Miscellanea|part=3|page=127|passage=[...] He ordered Her to '''call''' at His Houſe once a Week, which She did for ſome Time; after which He heard no more of Her.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=58|passage=The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to '''call''' at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track.}}
## To [[stop]] at a [[station]] or [[port]].
##: {{ux|en|This train '''calls''' at Reading, Slough and London Paddington.}}
##: {{ux|en|Our cruise ship '''called''' at Bristol Harbour.}}
## To [[come to pass]]; to [[afflict]].
##* {{RQ:Wonder Fool|passage=They say your love will surely fade, girl, / When things go wrong and trouble '''calls'''.}}
# {{lb|en|heading}} To [[name]], [[identify]]{{,}} or [[describe]].
## {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[name]] or refer to.
##: {{syn|en|designate|dub|name|Thesaurus:denominate}}
##: {{ux|en|Why don’t we dispense with the formalities? Please '''call''' me Al.}}
##: {{ux|en|Don't '''call''' me a liar.}}
##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=I don't know how you and the 'head,' as you '''call''' him, will get on, but I do know that if you '''call''' my duds a 'livery' again there'll be trouble. It's bad enough to go around togged out like a life saver on a drill day, but I can stand that 'cause I'm paid for it. What I won't stand is to have them togs '''called''' a livery.}}
##* {{RQ:Rinehart Hopwood Bat|chapter=The Shadow of the Bat|page=6|passage=The Bat—they '''called''' him the Bat. Like a bat he chose the night hours for his work of rapine; like a bat he struck and vanished, pouncingly, noiselessly; like a bat he never showed himself to the face of the day.}}
## {{lb|en|in passive}} Of a person, to have as one's name; of a thing, to have as its name.
##: {{ux|en|I’m '''called''' John.}}
##: {{ux|en|A very tall building is '''called''' a skyscraper.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=w:Henry Petroski|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/the-evolution-of-eyeglasses The Evolution of Eyeglasses]
|passage=The ability of a segment of a glass sphere to magnify whatever is placed before it was known around the year 1000, when the spherical segment was '''called''' a reading stone, essentially what today we might term a frameless magnifying glass or plain glass paperweight.}}
## To state, or estimate, approximately or loosely; to characterize without strict regard to fact.
##: {{ux|en|They '''call''' the distance ten miles.}}
##: {{ux|en|That’s enough work. Let's '''call''' it a day and go home.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1842|author=[[w:Henry Brougham, 1st Baron Brougham and Vaux|Henry Brougham]]|title=Political Philosophy
|passage=The whole army is '''called''' 700,000 men}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[claim]] the [[existence]] of some [[malfeasance]]; to [[denounce]] as.
##: {{ux|en|I '''call''' bullshit.}}
##: {{ux|en|She '''called''' foul on their scheme.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2008|journal=PC Magazine
|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=khZAAQAAIAAJ&q=%22called+shenanigans%22
|text=Having been around the block a few times, I immediately '''called''' "shenanigans” on it, but even so, I was taken aback.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To disclose the class or character of; to identify.
##* {{RQ:Beaumont Fletcher Comedies and Tragedies|folio=2nd|title=Philaster|act=I|scene=i|page=22|column=2|passage=This ſpeech '''calls''' him ''Spaniard'', being nothing but / A large inventory of his own commendations.}}
# {{lb|en|heading}} To [[declare]], or declare [[in favor of]], a [[predict]]ed or [[actual]] [[result]].
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[declare]] [[in advance]].
##: {{ux|en|The captains '''call''' the coin toss.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[predict]].
##: {{syn|en|augur|foretell|Thesaurus:predict}}
##: {{ux|en|He '''called''' twelve of the last three recessions.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To formally recognise a death: especially to announce and record the time, place and fact of a person’s death.
## To declare (an effort or project) to be a failure.
##: {{ux|en|After the third massive failure, John '''called''' the whole initiative.}}
## {{lb|en|sports}} To [[make]] a [[decision]] as a [[referee]] or [[umpire]].
##: {{ux|en|The goal was '''called''' offside.}}
# {{lb|en|heading|sport}} {{ng|Direct or indirect use of the voice.}}
## {{lb|en|cricket}} (of a [[batsman]]): To [[shout]] [[directions]] to the other batsman on [[whether]] or not they should take a run.
## {{lb|en|baseball|cricket}} (of a [[fielder]]): To shout to other fielders that he [[intend]]s to take a [[catch]] (thus [[avoid]]ing [[collision]]s).
## {{lb|en|cue sports}} To tell in advance which shot one is attempting.
##: {{syn|en|name|nominate|Thesaurus:specify}}
##: {{ux|en|Every shot must be '''called'''.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|poker}} To [[equal]] the same amount that other [[player]]s are currently betting.
##: {{ux|en|I bet $800 and Jane raised to $1600. My options: '''call''' (match her $1600 bet), reraise{{,}} or fold.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|poker|proscribed}} To [[match]] the current bet amount, in preparation for a [[raise]] in the same turn. (Usually, players are forbidden to announce one's play this way.)
##: {{ux|en|I’ll '''call''' your 300, and raise to 600!}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[state]], or invoke a [[rule]], in many games such as [[bridge]], [[craps]], [[jacks]], and so on.
##: {{ux|en|My partner '''called''' two spades.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|sometimes with ''for''}} To [[require]], [[demand#Verb|demand]].
#: {{ux|en|He felt '''called''' to help the old man.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|with ''into''}} To [[cause]] to be verbally [[subject]]ed to.
#* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=The Gateway, and Some Who Passed|page=29|passage=Carried somehow, somewhither, for some reason, on these surging floods, were these travelers, of errand not wholly obvious to their fellows, yet of such sort as to '''call''' into query alike the nature of their errand and their own relations.}}
#: {{ux|en|The basis for his conclusion was '''called''' into doubt}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[lay claim]] to an object or role which is [[up for grabs]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''call''' the comfy chair!}}
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1998|title=The Simpsons|season=9|episode=The Trouble with Trillions
|url=https://comb.io/NtuLNU
|text=Mr. Burns: Any of these islands would make a fine new country. / Homer: I '''call''' president! / Mr. Burns: Vice president! / Smithers: [groans]
}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|finance}} To [[announce]] the early [[extinction]] of a [[debt]] by [[prepayment]], usually at a [[premium]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|banking}} To [[demand]] [[repayment]] of a [[loan]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To [[jump]] to (another part of a [[program]]); to perform some [[operation]], returning to the original point on [[completion]].
#: {{ux|en|A recursive function is one that '''calls''' itself.}}

====Usage notes====
* In older forms of English, when the pronoun ''[[thou]]'' was in active use, and verbs used ''[[-est]]'' for distinct second-person singular indicative forms, the verb ''call'' had the form ''[[callest]]'', and had ''[[calledst]]'' for its past tense.
* Similarly, when the ending ''[[-eth]]'' was in active use for third-person singular present indicative forms, the form ''[[calleth]]'' was used.
* The sense of naming an object, as with the phrase ''it’s called a(n)'', is intended to humiliate a listener when the object is known to be familiar:
*: {{usex|en|Hey, here’s something to keep you dry in the rain. It’s '''called''' an umbrella.}}
